questions.instruction: Tell a short story about your family. Introduce your family members, say their names, and describe one good quality for each person. Use possessive 's and possessive adjectives (my, his, her). Speak for about 30 seconds.
questions.audioPrompt: Now it is your turn to tell me about your family. Please introduce at least three family members. Tell me their names and say something nice about each person. Use words like 'my', 'his', 'her', and possessive 's. For example, 'My sister's name is Ani. She is very clever.' Ready? Go ahead!
storyPoints: Introduce at least three family members by their relationship to you (for example: my mother, my father, my sister).
Use possessive 's to talk about each person's name or quality (for example: my brother's name, my father's job).
Describe one good quality for each family member using a simple adjective (for example: kind, helpful, clever, funny).
questions.targetSentence: My mother's name is Sari. She is very kind. My father's name is Budi. He is very helpful. My sister's name is Ani. She is really clever.
questions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈmʌðərz neɪm ɪz ˈsɑːri. ʃiː ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd. maɪ ˈfɑːðərz neɪm ɪz ˈbuːdi. hiː ɪz ˈveri ˈhelpfʊl. maɪ ˈsɪstərz neɪm ɪz ˈɑːni. ʃiː ɪz ˈrɪəli ˈklevər/
questions.hint: Remember to use possessive 's after the family member word: 'my mother's name', not 'my mother name'. Use falling intonation at the end of each statement.
questions.explanation: This storytelling task practises introducing family members using possessive 's (my mother's name) and possessive adjectives (my, his, her). It also practises using simple adjectives to describe people's good qualities, which is a key objective of this unit.

questions.instruction: Describe your family using demonstratives (this, that, these, those). Imagine you are showing a family photo to a friend. Point to each person and say who they are and what they are like.
questions.audioPrompt: Imagine you have a family photo. You are showing it to me. Please point to the people in the photo and tell me who they are. Use words like 'this is', 'that is', 'these are', and 'those are'. Describe each person with a nice adjective. Ready? Start now!
storyPoints: Use 'this is' or 'that is' to introduce individual family members in the photo.
Use 'these are' or 'those are' to introduce groups of family members (for example: these are my grandparents).
Give a simple compliment or describe a good quality for at least two people in the photo.
questions.targetSentence: This is my mother. She is very beautiful. That is my father. He is really strong. These are my grandparents. They are very kind and loving.
questions.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈmʌðər. ʃiː ɪz ˈveri ˈbjuːtɪfʊl. ðæt ɪz maɪ ˈfɑːðər. hiː ɪz ˈrɪəli strɒŋ. ðiːz ɑːr maɪ ˈɡrænpeərənts. ðeɪ ɑːr ˈveri kaɪnd ænd ˈlʌvɪŋ/
questions.hint: Remember the /ð/ sound at the beginning of 'this', 'that', 'these', and 'those'. Place your tongue between your teeth. Use falling intonation for statements.
questions.explanation: This task practises using demonstratives (this/that/these/those) to identify family members, combined with possessive adjectives and simple compliment adjectives. It reinforces the unit's focus on describing family and giving compliments.

questions.instruction: You receive a video call from Mr. Khoirul. He wants to meet your family. Introduce your family members one by one. Use possessive 's and possessive adjectives.
questions.audioPrompt: Ring ring! Hello, this is Mr. Khoirul calling! I would love to meet your family today. Can you introduce them to me one by one? Tell me their names and something nice about each person.
questions.scenarioContext: You are at home with your family. Mr. Khoirul, your English teacher, calls you on a video call. He is very friendly and curious about your family. You need to introduce your mother, father, and one sibling. For each person, say their name using possessive 's and describe one good quality.
questions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is a warm and encouraging English teacher. He asks simple follow-up questions like 'What is his name?' and 'Is she kind?' He speaks slowly and clearly at A1 level.
questions.targetSentence: This is my mother. Her name is Sari. She is very kind. This is my father. His name is Budi. He is really helpful.
questions.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈmʌðər. hɜːr neɪm ɪz ˈsɑːri. ʃiː ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd. ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈfɑːðər. hɪz neɪm ɪz ˈbuːdi. hiː ɪz ˈrɪəli ˈhelpfʊl/
questions.hint: When Mr. Khoirul asks 'What is her name?', answer with a full sentence: 'Her name is...' Do not just say the name alone.
questions.explanation: This roleplay practises real-time family introductions using possessive adjectives (my, his, her) and possessive 's in a natural conversation with a teacher.

questions.instruction: You are at school. A new classmate asks about your family. Answer the questions and ask about their family too. Use possessive adjectives and give compliments.
questions.audioPrompt: Hi! I am new in this class. My name is Rina. I want to know about your family. How many people are in your family? Tell me about them!
questions.scenarioContext: It is your first day back at school. A new student named Rina sits next to you. She is friendly and wants to get to know you. She asks about your family members, and you also ask about hers. You practise using possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her) and giving simple compliments.
questions.characterRole: Rina is a cheerful new classmate. She speaks simple English and asks questions like 'How many brothers do you have?' and 'What is your mother like?' She also shares information about her own family so you can respond with compliments.
questions.targetSentence: I have four people in my family. My father is a teacher. My mother is very kind. Your family sounds really nice!
questions.phonetic: /aɪ hæv fɔːr ˈpiːpəl ɪn maɪ ˈfæməli. maɪ ˈfɑːðər ɪz ə ˈtiːtʃər. maɪ ˈmʌðər ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd. jɔːr ˈfæməli saʊndz ˈrɪəli naɪs/
questions.hint: When Rina tells you about her family, respond with a compliment. For example: 'Your brother sounds very kind!' or 'That is really nice!'
questions.explanation: This roleplay practises two-way conversation about families, using possessive adjectives for both 'my' and 'your' family, and giving compliments to a peer.

questions.instruction: You are showing your family photo album to Mr. Khoirul. Use demonstratives (this, that, these, those) to point to people in the photos and describe them.
questions.audioPrompt: Oh, what a lovely photo album! Can you show me the photos? Please point to each person and tell me who they are. Use 'this is' for people close to you and 'that is' for people far away in the photo.
questions.scenarioContext: You are sitting with Mr. Khoirul and looking at your family photo album together. Some photos show people close up (use 'this') and some show people far away or in old photos (use 'that'). Group photos require 'these are' or 'those are'. Describe each person with a positive adjective.
questions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is looking at the photos with great interest. He asks questions like 'Who is this?' and 'Are those your cousins?' He encourages you to use full sentences and give compliments about the people in the photos.
questions.targetSentence: This is my sister. She is very clever. That is my grandfather. He is really funny. These are my cousins. They are very friendly.
questions.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈsɪstər. ʃiː ɪz ˈveri ˈklevər. ðæt ɪz maɪ ˈɡrænfɑːðər. hiː ɪz ˈrɪəli ˈfʌni. ðiːz ɑːr maɪ ˈkʌzənz. ðeɪ ɑːr ˈveri ˈfrendli/
questions.hint: Use 'this is' for one person near you, 'that is' for one person far away, 'these are' for a group near you, and 'those are' for a group far away. Always follow with a description.
questions.explanation: This roleplay specifically targets demonstrative pronouns (this/that/these/those) in the context of describing family members, combining them with possessive adjectives and compliment adjectives.

questions.instruction: You meet Mr. Khoirul at a school event. He introduces his family to you. Listen, respond politely, and then introduce your own family. Give compliments about his family members.
questions.audioPrompt: Hello! Welcome to the school event! I want to introduce my family to you. This is my wife. Her name is Dewi. She is a doctor. And this is my son. His name is Rafi. He is ten years old. Now, can you tell me about your family too?
questions.scenarioContext: You are at a school family day event. Mr. Khoirul introduces his wife and son to you. You need to respond with polite compliments about his family, and then introduce your own family members using possessive 's and possessive adjectives. This is a polite, semi-formal conversation.
questions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is proud of his family and introduces them warmly. He expects you to give a compliment about his wife or son, and then share about your own family. He may ask follow-up questions like 'What does your father do?' or 'Is your sister older or younger?'
questions.targetSentence: Nice to meet your family! Your wife is very kind. Your son is really smart. This is my mother. Her name is Sari. She is a wonderful cook.
questions.phonetic: /naɪs tuː miːt jɔːr ˈfæməli. jɔːr waɪf ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd. jɔːr sʌn ɪz ˈrɪəli smɑːrt. ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈmʌðər. hɜːr neɪm ɪz ˈsɑːri. ʃiː ɪz ə ˈwʌndərfʊl kʊk/
questions.hint: When someone introduces their family, always respond with a compliment first. Say 'Nice to meet your family!' or 'Your son is very smart!' before talking about your own family.
questions.explanation: This roleplay practises both receiving and giving family introductions, using 'your' for the other person's family and 'my/her/his' for your own. It also practises giving polite compliments in a semi-formal setting.

questions.instruction: Say the following family vocabulary words clearly. Focus on correct pronunciation of each word.
questions.audioPrompt: Let us practise family vocabulary. I will give you a word and you need to say it clearly. Ready? Please say the word: 'grandmother'.
questions.hint: This word has three syllables: GRAND-mo-ther. The stress is on the first syllable 'GRAND'. Make sure you pronounce the /ð/ sound in 'ther' by placing your tongue between your teeth.
questions.explanation: The word 'grandmother' is a compound family noun. At A1 level, learners need to master basic family vocabulary with correct syllable stress. The primary stress falls on 'GRAND', and the /ð/ in the final syllable is a key pronunciation target for this unit.

questions.instruction: Say the following sentence aloud. Pay attention to the correct use of possessive 's and the possessive adjective 'her'.
questions.audioPrompt: Now let us practise grammar in speaking. Please say this sentence clearly: 'My sister's favourite colour is blue. Her room is blue too.'
questions.targetSentence: My sister's favourite colour is blue. Her room is blue too.
questions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈsɪstərz ˈfeɪvərɪt ˈkʌlər ɪz bluː. hɜːr ruːm ɪz bluː tuː/
questions.hint: Notice two possessive forms here: 'sister's' uses apostrophe s to show that the favourite colour belongs to your sister. 'Her' is a possessive adjective that replaces 'my sister's' to avoid repetition. Say 'sister's favourite' as one smooth phrase.
questions.explanation: This drill targets two key grammar points from the unit: possessive 's (sister's favourite) and possessive adjectives (her room). Learners must produce both forms correctly in connected speech, showing they understand that 'her' refers back to 'my sister'.

questions.instruction: Say both words and notice how the syllable stress changes. First say 'brother', then say 'stepbrother'. Pay attention to which syllable is strongest.
questions.audioPrompt: Let us practise syllable stress with family words. First, say 'brother' — the stress is on 'BRO'. Now say 'stepbrother' — the stress moves to 'STEP'. Say both words: 'BRO-ther' and then 'STEP-bro-ther'. Can you feel the difference?
questions.hint: In 'brother', you stress the first syllable: BRO-ther. In 'stepbrother', the stress shifts to the prefix: STEP-bro-ther. The syllable 'bro' becomes weaker in the compound word. Tap your hand on the table on the stressed syllable to feel the rhythm.
questions.explanation: This drill practises syllable stress shift in compound family nouns. When 'brother' stands alone, it has primary stress on 'BRO'. When it becomes part of the compound 'stepbrother', the primary stress shifts to the prefix 'STEP', and 'brother' receives reduced stress. This pattern applies to many compound family words (grandmother, grandfather, stepsister).

questions.instruction: Say these two sentences with the correct intonation pattern. The first sentence is a yes/no question (rising intonation). The second sentence is a statement with a compliment (falling intonation).
questions.audioPrompt: Let us practise intonation. First, say this question with rising intonation — your voice goes UP at the end: 'Is that your sister?' Now say this compliment with falling intonation — your voice goes DOWN at the end: 'She is really beautiful!' Try both sentences now.
questions.targetSentence: Is that your sister? She is really beautiful!
questions.phonetic: /ɪz ðæt jɔːr ˈsɪstər↗ ʃiː ɪz ˈrɪəli ˈbjuːtɪfʊl↘/
questions.hint: For the question 'Is that your sister?', imagine your voice is climbing stairs — it goes UP at the end. For the compliment 'She is really beautiful!', imagine your voice is going down a slide — it goes DOWN at the end. The rising tone shows you are asking; the falling tone shows you are making a warm statement.
questions.explanation: This drill contrasts rising intonation (used in yes/no questions like 'Is that your sister?') with falling intonation (used in statements and compliments like 'She is really beautiful!'). Mastering this contrast is essential for natural English conversation about family, especially when asking about and complimenting family members.

practicumQuestions.question: In the passage, Lucia says: 'My mother's name is Ana.' What does the 's after 'mother' mean?
options: It shows possession — the name belongs to her mother.
practicumQuestions.answer: It shows possession — the name belongs to her mother.
practicumQuestions.explanation: When we write 'My mother's name,' the 's shows that the name belongs to her mother. This is the possessive 's. It is different from the contraction 'She's' (She is).

practicumQuestions.question: Lucia writes: 'His name is Pedro.' Who does 'His' refer to?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Just before this sentence, Lucia says: 'I have one brother.' Then she says: 'His name is Pedro.' The possessive adjective 'His' refers to the brother she just mentioned.

practicumQuestions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the possessive 's?
practicumQuestions.explanation: To show that the name belongs to the grandmother, we add 's after 'grandmother.' The correct form is 'My grandmother's name is Rosa.' Without the apostrophe and s, the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

practicumQuestions.question: Lucia says: 'This is my bedroom.' Why does she use 'this' and not 'that'?
options: Because the bedroom is near her — she is pointing to something close.
Because the bedroom is far away from her.
practicumQuestions.answer: Because the bedroom is near her — she is pointing to something close.
practicumQuestions.explanation: We use 'this' for something singular that is near us. Lucia is standing in or next to her bedroom, so she says 'This is my bedroom.' If it were far away, she would say 'That is my bedroom.'

practicumQuestions.question: Lucia writes: 'Those are their children — my cousins, Marco and Bianca.' Why does she use 'those' instead of 'this'?
options: Because she is talking about more than one person who are not right next to her.
Because she is talking about only one person who is near her.
Because 'those' is used for singular nouns.
practicumQuestions.answer: Because she is talking about more than one person who are not right next to her.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Those' is used for plural people or things that are farther away. Marco and Bianca are two people (plural), and they are not standing right next to Lucia. So 'those' is the correct word.

practicumQuestions.question: Which word correctly completes this sentence? '_______ is my aunt Sofia. She's very friendly.'
practicumQuestions.explanation: We need a singular demonstrative because we are talking about one person (Aunt Sofia). 'Those' and 'These' are for plural. 'That' is correct for one person who is not right next to the speaker.

practicumQuestions.question: According to the passage, which adjective describes Lucia's brother Pedro?
practicumQuestions.explanation: The passage says: 'Pedro is really helpful at home.' The adjective 'helpful' describes Pedro. 'Generous' describes the grandmother Rosa, and 'friendly' describes Aunt Sofia.

practicumQuestions.question: Read this sentence from the passage: 'She's my mother's mother.' What does this sentence tell us about Rosa?
options: Rosa is Lucia's grandmother on her mother's side.
practicumQuestions.answer: Rosa is Lucia's grandmother on her mother's side.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The sentence 'She's my mother's mother' means Rosa is the mother of Lucia's mother. That makes Rosa Lucia's grandmother. Notice the two possessive forms: 'my mother's' (belonging to my mother) and 'mother' (the person who is her mother).

practicumQuestions.question: Which sentence expresses a future plan?
options: I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
I visit my grandmother every day.
practicumQuestions.answer: I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Be going to' expresses a planned future intention.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write 3 sentences using possessive 's to talk about things that belong to your family members. For example, talk about your sister's phone, your father's car, or your mother's smile.
practicumQuestions.criteria: The response must contain at least 3 complete sentences. Each sentence must correctly use possessive 's attached to a person's name or family title (e.g., Maria's, my sister's). Sentences must have correct capitalization and punctuation.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: My mother's cooking is delicious. My father's car is very big. Sarah's room is clean and beautiful.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write a short paragraph (at least 5 sentences) about your family. Introduce at least two family members using demonstratives (this, that, these, those). Describe their good qualities and give at least two compliments. Use possessive adjectives and possessive 's.
practicumQuestions.criteria: The response must contain at least 5 complete sentences forming a coherent paragraph. The student must correctly use at least one demonstrative (this/that/these/those), at least two possessive adjectives (my, his, her, our, their), at least one possessive 's construction, and at least two compliments using positive adjectives. All sentences must have correct capitalization and end punctuation.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: This is my family. That is my father. His name is Ahmad. He is very strong and kind. This is my mother. Her name is Siti. My mother's smile is very beautiful. These are my sisters. Their names are Rina and Dewi. They are really smart and funny. I love my family very much.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tuliskan kalimat sopan meminta segelas air menggunakan 'Can I':
practicumQuestions.prompt: Ask politely for a glass of water.
practicumQuestions.hint: Can I have a glass of water, please?
targetAnswers: Can I have a glass of water, please?
Can I have a glass of water please?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Struktur standar permintaan sopan: Can I have + objek + please?

practicumQuestions.instruction: Ubah kalimat positif berikut menjadi bentuk negatif:
practicumQuestions.prompt: Mark works in an office downtown.
practicumQuestions.hint: Gunakan 'does not' atau 'doesn't' sebelum kata kerja.
targetAnswers: Mark doesn't work in an office downtown.
Mark does not work in an office downtown.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Dalam present simple, subjek orang ketiga tunggal menggunakan 'doesn't + base verb'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Ubah kalimat berikut ke bentuk Simple Past:
practicumQuestions.prompt: They go to the beach on Sundays.
practicumQuestions.hint: Bentuk lampau dari 'go' adalah 'went'.
targetAnswers: They went to the beach on Sunday.
They went to the beach.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Go' adalah kata kerja tidak beraturan yang berubah menjadi 'went' di waktu lampau.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Buat kalimat tanya dari kata-kata berikut:
practicumQuestions.hint: Awali dengan 'Do'.
targetAnswers: Do you like Italian food?
Do you like Italian food
practicumQuestions.explanation: Pola pertanyaan present simple: Do + you + like + objek?

practicumQuestions.instruction: Perbaiki kesalahan tata bahasa dalam kalimat ini:
practicumQuestions.prompt: She don't have any brothers or sisters.
practicumQuestions.hint: Subjek 'she' harus dipasangkan dengan 'doesn't'.
targetAnswers: She doesn't have any brothers or sisters.
She does not have any brothers or sisters.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'She' memerlukan auxiliary 'doesn't', bukan 'don't'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Lengkapi kalimat dengan bentuk present continuous dari kata kerja 'cook':
practicumQuestions.prompt: Right now, my mother _____ dinner in the kitchen.
practicumQuestions.hint: Gunakan 'is' + verb-ing.
targetAnswers: is cooking
My mother is cooking dinner in the kitchen.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Present continuous untuk subjek tunggal menggunakan 'is + verb-ing'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Susun kata-kata ini menjadi kalimat yang benar:
practicumQuestions.prompt: never / late / He / is / for / school
practicumQuestions.hint: Kata keterangan frekuensi 'never' diletakkan setelah to be 'is'.
targetAnswers: He is never late for school.
He is never late for school
practicumQuestions.explanation: Adverb of frequency diletakkan setelah to be: He is never late for school.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tell a short story about your family. Introduce your family members, say their names, and describe one good quality for each person. Use possessive 's and possessive adjectives (my, his, her). Speak for about 30 seconds.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Now it is your turn to tell me about your family. Please introduce at least three family members. Tell me their names and say something nice about each person. Use words like 'my', 'his', 'her', and possessive 's. For example, 'My sister's name is Ani. She is very clever.' Ready? Go ahead!
storyPoints: Introduce at least three family members by their relationship to you (for example: my mother, my father, my sister).
Use possessive 's to talk about each person's name or quality (for example: my brother's name, my father's job).
Describe one good quality for each family member using a simple adjective (for example: kind, helpful, clever, funny).
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My mother's name is Sari. She is very kind. My father's name is Budi. He is very helpful. My sister's name is Ani. She is really clever.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈmʌðərz neɪm ɪz ˈsɑːri. ʃiː ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd. maɪ ˈfɑːðərz neɪm ɪz ˈbuːdi. hiː ɪz ˈveri ˈhelpfʊl. maɪ ˈsɪstərz neɪm ɪz ˈɑːni. ʃiː ɪz ˈrɪəli ˈklevər/
practicumQuestions.hint: Remember to use possessive 's after the family member word: 'my mother's name', not 'my mother name'. Use falling intonation at the end of each statement.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This storytelling task practises introducing family members using possessive 's (my mother's name) and possessive adjectives (my, his, her). It also practises using simple adjectives to describe people's good qualities, which is a key objective of this unit.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Describe your family using demonstratives (this, that, these, those). Imagine you are showing a family photo to a friend. Point to each person and say who they are and what they are like.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Imagine you have a family photo. You are showing it to me. Please point to the people in the photo and tell me who they are. Use words like 'this is', 'that is', 'these are', and 'those are'. Describe each person with a nice adjective. Ready? Start now!
storyPoints: Use 'this is' or 'that is' to introduce individual family members in the photo.
Use 'these are' or 'those are' to introduce groups of family members (for example: these are my grandparents).
Give a simple compliment or describe a good quality for at least two people in the photo.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: This is my mother. She is very beautiful. That is my father. He is really strong. These are my grandparents. They are very kind and loving.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈmʌðər. ʃiː ɪz ˈveri ˈbjuːtɪfʊl. ðæt ɪz maɪ ˈfɑːðər. hiː ɪz ˈrɪəli strɒŋ. ðiːz ɑːr maɪ ˈɡrænpeərənts. ðeɪ ɑːr ˈveri kaɪnd ænd ˈlʌvɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.hint: Remember the /ð/ sound at the beginning of 'this', 'that', 'these', and 'those'. Place your tongue between your teeth. Use falling intonation for statements.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This task practises using demonstratives (this/that/these/those) to identify family members, combined with possessive adjectives and simple compliment adjectives. It reinforces the unit's focus on describing family and giving compliments.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You receive a video call from Mr. Khoirul. He wants to meet your family. Introduce your family members one by one. Use possessive 's and possessive adjectives.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Ring ring! Hello, this is Mr. Khoirul calling! I would love to meet your family today. Can you introduce them to me one by one? Tell me their names and something nice about each person.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are at home with your family. Mr. Khoirul, your English teacher, calls you on a video call. He is very friendly and curious about your family. You need to introduce your mother, father, and one sibling. For each person, say their name using possessive 's and describe one good quality.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is a warm and encouraging English teacher. He asks simple follow-up questions like 'What is his name?' and 'Is she kind?' He speaks slowly and clearly at A1 level.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: This is my mother. Her name is Sari. She is very kind. This is my father. His name is Budi. He is really helpful.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈmʌðər. hɜːr neɪm ɪz ˈsɑːri. ʃiː ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd. ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈfɑːðər. hɪz neɪm ɪz ˈbuːdi. hiː ɪz ˈrɪəli ˈhelpfʊl/
practicumQuestions.hint: When Mr. Khoirul asks 'What is her name?', answer with a full sentence: 'Her name is...' Do not just say the name alone.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises real-time family introductions using possessive adjectives (my, his, her) and possessive 's in a natural conversation with a teacher.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are at school. A new classmate asks about your family. Answer the questions and ask about their family too. Use possessive adjectives and give compliments.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hi! I am new in this class. My name is Rina. I want to know about your family. How many people are in your family? Tell me about them!
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: It is your first day back at school. A new student named Rina sits next to you. She is friendly and wants to get to know you. She asks about your family members, and you also ask about hers. You practise using possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her) and giving simple compliments.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: Rina is a cheerful new classmate. She speaks simple English and asks questions like 'How many brothers do you have?' and 'What is your mother like?' She also shares information about her own family so you can respond with compliments.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I have four people in my family. My father is a teacher. My mother is very kind. Your family sounds really nice!
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ hæv fɔːr ˈpiːpəl ɪn maɪ ˈfæməli. maɪ ˈfɑːðər ɪz ə ˈtiːtʃər. maɪ ˈmʌðər ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd. jɔːr ˈfæməli saʊndz ˈrɪəli naɪs/
practicumQuestions.hint: When Rina tells you about her family, respond with a compliment. For example: 'Your brother sounds very kind!' or 'That is really nice!'
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises two-way conversation about families, using possessive adjectives for both 'my' and 'your' family, and giving compliments to a peer.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are showing your family photo album to Mr. Khoirul. Use demonstratives (this, that, these, those) to point to people in the photos and describe them.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Oh, what a lovely photo album! Can you show me the photos? Please point to each person and tell me who they are. Use 'this is' for people close to you and 'that is' for people far away in the photo.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are sitting with Mr. Khoirul and looking at your family photo album together. Some photos show people close up (use 'this') and some show people far away or in old photos (use 'that'). Group photos require 'these are' or 'those are'. Describe each person with a positive adjective.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is looking at the photos with great interest. He asks questions like 'Who is this?' and 'Are those your cousins?' He encourages you to use full sentences and give compliments about the people in the photos.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: This is my sister. She is very clever. That is my grandfather. He is really funny. These are my cousins. They are very friendly.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈsɪstər. ʃiː ɪz ˈveri ˈklevər. ðæt ɪz maɪ ˈɡrænfɑːðər. hiː ɪz ˈrɪəli ˈfʌni. ðiːz ɑːr maɪ ˈkʌzənz. ðeɪ ɑːr ˈveri ˈfrendli/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'this is' for one person near you, 'that is' for one person far away, 'these are' for a group near you, and 'those are' for a group far away. Always follow with a description.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay specifically targets demonstrative pronouns (this/that/these/those) in the context of describing family members, combining them with possessive adjectives and compliment adjectives.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You meet Mr. Khoirul at a school event. He introduces his family to you. Listen, respond politely, and then introduce your own family. Give compliments about his family members.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hello! Welcome to the school event! I want to introduce my family to you. This is my wife. Her name is Dewi. She is a doctor. And this is my son. His name is Rafi. He is ten years old. Now, can you tell me about your family too?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are at a school family day event. Mr. Khoirul introduces his wife and son to you. You need to respond with polite compliments about his family, and then introduce your own family members using possessive 's and possessive adjectives. This is a polite, semi-formal conversation.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is proud of his family and introduces them warmly. He expects you to give a compliment about his wife or son, and then share about your own family. He may ask follow-up questions like 'What does your father do?' or 'Is your sister older or younger?'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Nice to meet your family! Your wife is very kind. Your son is really smart. This is my mother. Her name is Sari. She is a wonderful cook.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /naɪs tuː miːt jɔːr ˈfæməli. jɔːr waɪf ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd. jɔːr sʌn ɪz ˈrɪəli smɑːrt. ðɪs ɪz maɪ ˈmʌðər. hɜːr neɪm ɪz ˈsɑːri. ʃiː ɪz ə ˈwʌndərfʊl kʊk/
practicumQuestions.hint: When someone introduces their family, always respond with a compliment first. Say 'Nice to meet your family!' or 'Your son is very smart!' before talking about your own family.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises both receiving and giving family introductions, using 'your' for the other person's family and 'my/her/his' for your own. It also practises giving polite compliments in a semi-formal setting.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following family vocabulary words clearly. Focus on correct pronunciation of each word.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Let us practise family vocabulary. I will give you a word and you need to say it clearly. Ready? Please say the word: 'grandmother'.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: grandmother
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈɡrænmʌðər/
practicumQuestions.hint: This word has three syllables: GRAND-mo-ther. The stress is on the first syllable 'GRAND'. Make sure you pronounce the /ð/ sound in 'ther' by placing your tongue between your teeth.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The word 'grandmother' is a compound family noun. At A1 level, learners need to master basic family vocabulary with correct syllable stress. The primary stress falls on 'GRAND', and the /ð/ in the final syllable is a key pronunciation target for this unit.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence aloud. Pay attention to the correct use of possessive 's and the possessive adjective 'her'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Now let us practise grammar in speaking. Please say this sentence clearly: 'My sister's favourite colour is blue. Her room is blue too.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My sister's favourite colour is blue. Her room is blue too.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈsɪstərz ˈfeɪvərɪt ˈkʌlər ɪz bluː. hɜːr ruːm ɪz bluː tuː/
practicumQuestions.hint: Notice two possessive forms here: 'sister's' uses apostrophe s to show that the favourite colour belongs to your sister. 'Her' is a possessive adjective that replaces 'my sister's' to avoid repetition. Say 'sister's favourite' as one smooth phrase.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill targets two key grammar points from the unit: possessive 's (sister's favourite) and possessive adjectives (her room). Learners must produce both forms correctly in connected speech, showing they understand that 'her' refers back to 'my sister'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say both words and notice how the syllable stress changes. First say 'brother', then say 'stepbrother'. Pay attention to which syllable is strongest.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Let us practise syllable stress with family words. First, say 'brother' — the stress is on 'BRO'. Now say 'stepbrother' — the stress moves to 'STEP'. Say both words: 'BRO-ther' and then 'STEP-bro-ther'. Can you feel the difference?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: brother, stepbrother
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈbrʌðər/ → /ˈstepbrʌðər/
practicumQuestions.hint: In 'brother', you stress the first syllable: BRO-ther. In 'stepbrother', the stress shifts to the prefix: STEP-bro-ther. The syllable 'bro' becomes weaker in the compound word. Tap your hand on the table on the stressed syllable to feel the rhythm.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill practises syllable stress shift in compound family nouns. When 'brother' stands alone, it has primary stress on 'BRO'. When it becomes part of the compound 'stepbrother', the primary stress shifts to the prefix 'STEP', and 'brother' receives reduced stress. This pattern applies to many compound family words (grandmother, grandfather, stepsister).

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say these two sentences with the correct intonation pattern. The first sentence is a yes/no question (rising intonation). The second sentence is a statement with a compliment (falling intonation).
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Let us practise intonation. First, say this question with rising intonation — your voice goes UP at the end: 'Is that your sister?' Now say this compliment with falling intonation — your voice goes DOWN at the end: 'She is really beautiful!' Try both sentences now.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Is that your sister? She is really beautiful!
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪz ðæt jɔːr ˈsɪstər↗ ʃiː ɪz ˈrɪəli ˈbjuːtɪfʊl↘/
practicumQuestions.hint: For the question 'Is that your sister?', imagine your voice is climbing stairs — it goes UP at the end. For the compliment 'She is really beautiful!', imagine your voice is going down a slide — it goes DOWN at the end. The rising tone shows you are asking; the falling tone shows you are making a warm statement.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill contrasts rising intonation (used in yes/no questions like 'Is that your sister?') with falling intonation (used in statements and compliments like 'She is really beautiful!'). Mastering this contrast is essential for natural English conversation about family, especially when asking about and complimenting family members.

practicumQuestions.sampleAnswer: I really love spicy food, but I do not like sugary drinks.
